subject.title: Gateway runtime: "no such table: plugin_state_entries / acp_sessions" despite tables existing in state/openclaw.sqlite (agent turns produce no reply)

question: Should maintainers require redacted runtime path diagnostics before starting a fix, or is the paired table-error report enough to sponsor a Docker repro/fix branch now?
rationale: The source paths are clear, but the reported contradiction depends on which SQLite file the live Docker process opens; choosing a repair without that proof could add recovery behavior in the wrong layer.

options.title: Collect path proof first
options.body: Ask for redacted `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, resolved shared DB path, and `PRAGMA database_list` output from the failing gateway process before selecting the fix boundary.

options.title: Sponsor a Docker repro branch
options.body: Treat the report as enough signal to build a Docker repro that exercises gateway run, device-pair notify polling, `chat.history`, and `sessions.send` under the stated env.

options.title: Fold into broader state recovery
options.body: Use this only if maintainers decide the table errors are part of a larger shared SQLite recovery program rather than a distinct path inconsistency.

recommendation.title: Collect path proof first
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, resolved shared DB path, and `PRAGMA database_list` output from the failing gateway process before selecting the fix boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The deepest feature-history signal for shared SQLite state and ACP metadata persistence points to steipete's commits.
